unit-m3nl.title: Topic 3 · Decimals on the Number Line
unit-m3nl.srcName: Topic 3 (enVision G4) — place value and decimals, Drive

summary.text: Twelve decimals to place on a number line by dragging a marker: tenths on a line from 0 to 1, hundredths on zoomed-in lines, and two lines whose marks are halves rather than tenths. Right means within a hair of the spot.

why.text: Knowing where a decimal LIVES is different from reading it. Placing numbers on a line is the single best-evidenced way to build number sense, and it is exactly what comparing and rounding decimals rest on.

objectives.text: Place a decimal to the tenths on a number line.
Place a decimal to the hundredths on a zoomed-in line.
Work out what one space is worth when the marks are not tenths.

parentNote.text: A new question type: she drags a marker along a number line instead of picking an option, and the app checks whether she landed within a small tolerance of the right spot (about a third of a space). Two lines use halves rather than tenths as their marks, on purpose — the trap is counting marks without first asking what each one is worth, which is the same trap as reading a cylinder. The hundredths questions zoom the line in (0.3 to 0.4, say) so a thumb-width is never the difference between right and wrong on a phone. Never served in Beat the clock — dragging against a countdown tests dragging.

nextUp.text: Twelve drags. Look at the labels before you touch the marker, and say the number out loud as you land it.

cards.term: A number line is a ruler for numbers
cards.def:
**Every number has exactly one place on the line, and the space between two labelled marks is split into equal parts.**
• 0.5 sits exactly halfway between 0 and 1.
• Bigger is always further right.
cards.hint: Half of the way is half of the number.

cards.term: Tenths split a whole into ten
cards.def:
**Between 0 and 1 there are ten equal spaces; each one is a tenth (0.1).**
• 0.3 is three spaces along from 0.
• 2.6 is six spaces along from 2.
cards.hint: Count the spaces, not the marks.

cards.term: Hundredths split a tenth into ten
cards.def:
**Zoom in on one tenth and it splits into ten hundredths (0.01 each).**
• 0.34 is four hundredths past 0.3 — almost halfway to 0.4.
• 0.07 is seven hundredths past 0 — most of the way to 0.1.
cards.hint: Two decimal places means you are counting the small spaces.

cards.term: When the marks are not tenths
cards.def:
**Work out what one space is worth first: the gap between two labels ÷ the number of spaces.**
• On a line from 0 to 2 with four spaces, each space is 0.5.
• Then count spaces from the label just below your number.
cards.hint: Same rule as reading a thermometer or a cylinder.

questions.hint: Half of one is halfway along.
steps: 0.5 is five tenths — halfway between 0 and 1.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.5 sits exactly halfway between 0 and 1.** Five of the ten spaces.
ex.tip: A decimal ending in 5 is always a halfway point of something.

questions.hint: Three tenths, and then halfway to the fourth.
steps: 0.35 is three tenths plus half of a tenth.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.35 is halfway between 0.3 and 0.4.** Three full spaces, then half a space more.
ex.tip: Say it as “thirty-five hundredths” and the picture appears.

steps: 0.8 is eight tenths — two spaces short of 1.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.8 is eight tenths along — two spaces before 1.** Counting back from 1 is quicker here.
ex.tip: Near the top of the line, count down from the top label.

questions.hint: The whole number tells you which line; the tenths tell you where on it.
steps: 2.6 is 2 and six tenths — six spaces past 2.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **2.6 is six tenths past 2.** Just past the halfway mark at 2.5.
ex.tip: The line runs from 2 to 3, so the digit before the point is already handled.

questions.hint: A quarter of the way from 7 to 8.
steps: 7.25 is two tenths past 7, then half of the next tenth.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **7.25 is a quarter of the way from 7 to 8** — halfway between 7.2 and 7.3.
ex.tip: 0.25 is a quarter: the same as 25 cents in a dollar.

questions.q: Place 0.07 on the line from 0 to 0.1.
questions.hint: This line is one tenth long, so its spaces are hundredths.
steps: 0.07 is seven hundredths — seven spaces along a line of ten hundredths.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.07 is seven hundredths, seven spaces past 0 on a line that ends at 0.1.** Most of the way along.
ex.tip: A zoomed-in line: the whole thing is only one tenth.

questions.q: Place 0.34 on the line from 0.3 to 0.4.
questions.hint: The line starts at 0.3, so only the hundredths digit is left to place.
steps: 0.34 is four hundredths past 0.3.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.34 is four spaces past 0.3 on a line split into hundredths.** Just short of the halfway mark at 0.35.
ex.tip: Start from the left label — the tenths are already done for you.

questions.q: Place 5.18 on the line from 5.1 to 5.2.
steps: 5.18 is eight hundredths past 5.10.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **5.18 is eight spaces past 5.1, two spaces before 5.2.** Counting back from 5.2 is quicker.
ex.tip: Zoomed-in lines make hundredths as easy as tenths.

questions.q: Place 0.9 on the line from 0 to 2.
questions.hint: This line is two whole numbers long — 1 is in the middle.
steps: 0.9 is just short of 1, which is the middle of this line.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.9 is one tenth short of 1, and 1 is the middle of a line from 0 to 2.** Just left of centre.
ex.tip: Find the whole number first, then nudge.

questions.q: Place 1.75 on the line from 0 to 2.
questions.hint: The marks here are halves, not tenths.
steps: 1.75 is three quarters of the way from 1 to 2.
Find the label just below the number, then count spaces.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **1.75 is halfway between the 1.5 mark and 2.** Each mark on this line is worth 0.5, so 1.75 is half a space past the third mark.
ex.tip: Work out what one space is worth before you count.

questions.q: Place the decimal that is exactly halfway between 0.6 and 0.7.
questions.hint: Halfway between two tenths is a hundredths number.
steps: Halfway between 0.6 and 0.7 is 0.65.
Six full spaces, then half a space.
Drag the marker there and place it.

ex.main: **0.65 is halfway between 0.6 and 0.7.** Six tenths and five hundredths.
ex.tip: Between any two tenths, the halfway point ends in 5.

questions.q: Round 3.48 to the nearest tenth, and place the answer on the line.
questions.hint: Look at the hundredths digit to decide which tenth is nearer.
steps: 3.48 sits between 3.4 and 3.5.
The hundredths digit is 8, so it rounds up.
3.48 rounds to 3.5 — place the marker on the halfway mark.

ex.main: **3.48 rounds to 3.5.** The 8 in the hundredths place pushes it up to the next tenth — and 3.5 is the halfway mark of this line.
ex.tip: Rounding and placing are the same skill: which mark is nearest?
